news.title: Tuchel should listen to ‘the 0.1%’ and learn from England’s World Cup mistakes | Jacob Steinberg
news.lede: Head coach is keen to focus on positives but Nations League squad hints at desire for greater tactical options. Thomas Tuchel should be listening to the 0.1%. As he unveiled his first England squad since the World Cup, he said 99.9% of supporters he bumped into did not talk about his substitutions during the Argentina game. According to him, the conversation is far more positive.

news.title: Shafaq News..Iraq drawn with Egypt in FIFA U-15 World Cup
news.lede: Iraq was drawn in Group S alongside Egypt, the Cayman Islands, Macau, Saint Kitts and Nevis, and Trinidad and Tobago for the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival in Azerbaijan next month. The tournament will be held in Baku in late October, with 191 FIFA member associations taking part in an 8 versus 8 format. Teams will first compete in groups before being placed into six performance tiers based on their results, with the Tier A winner crowned champion. Matches will consist of two 20-minute halves, with each team playing four or five group-stage matches followed by another four or five games in the second stage.

news.title: Hans-Joachim Watzke reveals that he considered making Thomas Tuchel Germany coach after 2022 World Cup
news.lede: It seems Germany could have had a change in coach sooner after the 2022 FIFA World Cup. Hans-Joachim Watzke, vice-president of the German Football Association (DFB), revealed to Sky Sport (as captured by @iMiaSanMia) that after Germany’s group stage exit in Qatar, he had considered replacing then-national coach Hansi Flick with Thomas Tuchel. Tuchel was without a job at the time after being sacked by Chelsea. We were knocked out quite miserably in Qatar.

news.title: Infantino ‘must go’, says German FA vice-president
news.lede: The German Football Association was one of the few federations not to sign a letter supporting Gianni Infantino's re-election as Fifa president. (EPA Images pic) MINICH: Gianni Infantino must leave the Fifa presidency "no ifs or buts", according to Hans-Joachim Watzke, one of the vice-presidents of the German Football Association (DFB), as he spoke at a festival dedicated to artificial intelligence in Berlin on Thursday evening. The DFB was one of the few federations not to sign a letter of support for Infantino's re-election as Fifa president in six months' time. "He has to go, no ifs or buts," declared Hans-Joachim Watzke, who said that three points in particular counted against the Swiss.
